# LLMify AG

> Sovereign AI for Switzerland. LLMify AG builds and operates Kontexus, an AI workspace hosted in Switzerland: an agent that does real work inside a company's own documents and applications, connected to the Swiss software an SME already runs, with no dependency on US cloud providers.

LLMify AG is based in Cham, Zug, Switzerland, and is recognised by ETH Zurich as *A Start-up Company of ETH Zurich* (since 20 May 2026). The product is Kontexus, described at https://llmify.ch/#produkt. The application itself runs at https://kontexus.ch, where the entry page is a sign-in form rather than a description.

Last updated: 12 August 2026.

## Product: Kontexus

Kontexus is an AI agent with its own computer. It does not answer questions about documents from a distance; it opens them, edits them, files them and books the result into the systems a Swiss SME already runs.

- **The agent**: works on real files in a workspace, shows every step it takes, and asks instead of guessing when a document is ambiguous.
- **Connections**: Microsoft 365 (Outlook, Teams, OneDrive, SharePoint, Outlook Calendar), bexio, Abacus, plus Swiss legal sources (Fedlex, Entscheidsuche). Approvals are granted per operation, not per application.
- **Where it runs**: primarily as SaaS operated by LLMify with a Swiss provider. On request as a dedicated private cloud instance or fully on-premise behind the customer's own firewall.

## Pricing

Per user and month, including a monthly credit balance that covers tokens, storage and paid connections. Credits are pooled across the team.

- Start: CHF 60 per user per month, 2'000 credits
- Team: CHF 120 per user per month, 4'500 credits
- Pro: CHF 200 per user per month, 8'000 credits
- Enterprise: dedicated cloud instance or on-premise, unlimited users, own models on request. By arrangement.

Indicative prices, excluding VAT.

## Use cases shown on the site

- **Fiduciary**: pulling Q3 creditor invoices out of Outlook, filing them, assigning the three Swiss VAT rates (8.1% standard, 3.8% accommodation, 2.6% reduced) and SME chart-of-accounts codes, booking them in bexio, and flagging a wrong VAT rate rather than copying it.
- **Law firm**: checking the citations in a legal brief against Entscheidsuche and Fedlex and reporting which ones do not hold.
- **Sales**: answering a question raised in a Teams channel from the mail history, the quote in SharePoint and the open items in bexio, replying in the same thread.

These are demonstrations. Company names, invoice numbers and amounts are invented.

## Insights (German)

- [Open-Source-Modelle sind konkurrenzfähig](https://llmify.ch/insights/open-source-modelle/): Qwen 3.5 and Nemotron 3 Super both reach the 120B class and run on own infrastructure without API dependency.
- [KI unter US-Jurisdiktion](https://llmify.ch/insights/us-recht-ki-daten/): The CLOUD Act reaches data held in Switzerland by US providers. The proposed Remote Access Security Act could extend export controls to cloud AI.
- [Souveränität in der Praxis](https://llmify.ch/insights/souveraenitaet-praxis/): The ICC lost access to Microsoft services and moved to open source; the EU Parliament disabled AI features on all devices. Two cases where digital dependency became concrete.
